sources.title: DuckDB CSV Auto Detection
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling current documentation; exact DuckDB engine/documentation build is not displayed.
sources.locator: Sample Size; Detection Steps; default sample-size and file-seekability behavior.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official DuckDB documentation; inspected sample_size default, sample_size=-1, seekable versus non-seekable sampling, and detected dialect options.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Type detection defaults to 20,480 rows; sample_size=-1 reads the entire file for sampling. Seekable regular files can be sampled at different locations; non-seekable inputs such as gzip/stdin are sampled from the beginning.
sources.applicability: Supports provisional detection only. A full-file sampling setting is distinct from applying and validating the confirmed profile against every row.

sources.title: SQLite Transaction
sources.version_or_commit: SQLite official language documentation; rolling page, no version-specific snapshot shown.
sources.locator: Read transactions versus write transactions; DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE; Implicit versus explicit transactions, COMMIT behavior.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official SQLite documentation; inspected writer concurrency, transaction upgrade behavior, and SQLITE_BUSY at COMMIT.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Only one simultaneous write transaction is supported. A DEFERRED read transaction may fail to upgrade to a writer with SQLITE_BUSY; COMMIT may return SQLITE_BUSY and leave the transaction active.
sources.applicability: The import must define a bounded busy/retry or explicit rollback path and confirm commit/rollback state; concurrent changes require recomputing preview decisions.

sources.title: SQLite ON CONFLICT Clause
sources.version_or_commit: SQLite official language documentation; page states last updated 2025-11-22; no engine build is specified.
sources.locator: ABORT, FAIL, IGNORE, and REPLACE conflict-resolution algorithms.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official SQLite documentation; compared statement-level effects of each conflict algorithm.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: ABORT is default and backs out only the current statement while preserving prior transaction statements; FAIL can preserve earlier row changes in the failing statement; IGNORE skips affected rows; REPLACE deletes conflicting rows before insert.
sources.applicability: All-or-nothing import requires the application to explicitly roll back the outer transaction after an apply failure; the default statement conflict behavior alone is insufficient.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging and WAL-reset bug history
sources.version_or_commit: Official page last updated 2026-08-25; identifies fix in SQLite 3.51.3 and later, with backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7.
sources.locator: Overview, transaction atomicity across ATTACHed databases; Section 11, WAL-Reset Bug and its conditions/fixed versions.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official SQLite WAL page; inspected journal-mode scope, multi-database atomicity exception, affected versions, fixed releases, and required concurrency conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL-reset defect affects WAL databases through 3.51.2 and requires at least two connections to the same database plus coincident write/checkpoint activity. WAL transactions across multiple ATTACHed databases are not atomic as a set. Rollback-journal mode is SQLite default.
sources.applicability: Keep the release floor conditional on WAL and the supported connection pattern; if WAL is selected, pin a fixed version/backport and test. Keep all accepted rows and provenance in one database file if the design promises atomicity.
